title: Coproducts in an abelian derived category with K-injective resolutions
statement: Let C be an abelian category with an ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and assume every cochain complex has a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. If C has coproducts indexed by every set in universe s, then D(C) has coproducts of the same size. No AB4 or Grothendieck hypothesis is required once the K-injective resolution hypothesis is given.

source.place: Lemma 19.13.4, clauses (1)-(2), and its Hom computation; the proof only uses the explicitly assumed coproducts and K-injective resolutions

proof.text: Choose a complex K_i representing each object E_i of D(C), using essential surjectivity of DerivedCategory.Q. Form the degreewise coproduct K = coproduct K_i, which is a cochain complex because coproducts in the cochain-complex category are computed degreewise.

For any target Y choose a K-injective resolution L and identify Y with Q(L). Morphisms to Q(L) are chain maps modulo homotopy, by the K-injective localization Hom bijection. The already-proved generic private helpers derived_map_surjective and derived_map_homotopy in Sheaf.CategoryTheory.DerivedModuleDirectSums implement these two consequences without specializing C to modules.

Assemble any family of chain maps K_i to L into a unique chain map from K using Sigma.desc. If two derived maps from K agree on the coprojections, represent them by chain maps to L; their restrictions are homotopic. Assemble these homotopies degreewise by coproduct_homotopy (the generic proved helper in DerivedModuleDirectSums) to conclude the derived maps are equal. This proves the universal property for Q(K).
Transport its coprojections by the isomorphisms Q(K_i) to E_i, and apply hasCoproducts_of_colimit_cofans for every indexing type. The construction includes the empty family.
